summary: The article profiles local artisans who have adopted digital technology in weaving, blacksmithing, ceramics, lighting design, woodworking and fiber art between September 2023 and March 2024. Each craftsperson says the tools enhance rather than replace traditional skill, bringing speed, precision, less waste and new markets. The piece concludes that the future of local crafts lies in adapting and innovating while honoring heritage.
one_line: Local artisans in textiles, metalwork, ceramics, lighting, woodcraft and fiber art are blending traditional skills with CAD, robotics, 3D printing, CNC and VR.
key_facts: Marianne O'Donnell, a weaver in the small town of Redale, was visited on October 15, 2023; she uses digital interfaces and CAD software with her looms.
Marianne O'Donnell says designs that once took days to interpret onto the loom are now mapped out within hours, and loom sensors maintain thread tension to prevent errors.
Blacksmith Alexei Kuznetsov was visited on November 12, 2023; a robotic arm assists him with hammering heated metal.
Alexei Kuznetsov uses a new milling machine that etches detailed patterns onto metal, which he says opens up new markets for custom metalwork.
Ceramicist Emilia Rodriguez of the coastal town of Littleshore uses 3D printing to prototype designs faster, observed on December 3, 2023.
Emilia Rodriguez says testing designs digitally before touching clay has drastically reduced material waste and is cost-effective and environmentally friendly.
Lighting designer Aiden McClure installed his latest project on January 20, 2024: smart lamps that are voice-activated, color-changing, and made with hand-blown glass.
Woodworker Thomas Bennett combines CNC routers with hand-finishing techniques; on February 8, 2024 he explained how this helps replicate and restore antique woodwork.
Fiber artist Zoe Nguyen incorporates virtual reality into her exhibitions; her gallery show on March 15, 2024 lets visitors step into the story behind each piece with a headset.
Zoe Nguyen also uses VR to workshop designs in three-dimensional space before they are physically made.
The article covers practices after September 1, 2023, based on interviews with local artisans and craft professionals.
